title: Controlled decommissioning: compatibility validator and staged migration assistant
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an automated, auditable workflow to safely decommission old model variants while minimizing customer disruption. Deliverables: a compatibility validator service that scores customer workloads against candidate replacement models; an in-console staged migration assistant that suggests pins, SDK compatibility shims, and rollout windows; standardized customer notices and automated signal-driven scheduling for phased retirements.
background: We frequently onboard new model variants and need a reproducible, low-touch way to retire older weights without breaking customers who relied on subtle behavior differences.
Existing playbooks are fragmented across PM guides and engineering runbooks; customers occasionally hit silent regressions after model swaps or get surprised by sudden EoL notices.
Goal: reduce manual ops required from Solutions/Success teams and provide data-driven migration recommendations tied to published performance profiles.
goals: Provide a compatibility score (0-100) per customer workload comparing retiring variant -> candidate replacement using eval prompt suites and embedding drift metrics.
Expose an in-console migration assistant that surfaces low-risk & high-risk customers and generates migration suggestions (pin, gradual rollout, compatibility shim).
Automate customer-facing notices with templated content and link directly to migration guides and SDK warnings.
Publish performance profile diffs prominently in model catalog to make trade-offs explicit.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility validator returns a reproducible score and top 3 error classes for a sample of 50 production customers within the test org and matches manual evals >80% of the time.
Console shows a staged migration plan with one-click pin recommendations and a canary rollout policy for at least two model pairs.
Automated email notice templates and API warning headers are approved by Legal and Customer Success and can be scheduled from the console UI.
Telemetry: 90% of customers targeted by the assistant either accept a recommended pin or schedule a rollout within 30 days during the beta.
high_level_solution: Compatibility validator: batch-run historical prompt/response pairs (or synthetic eval suites) against retiring variant and candidate replacements; compute semantic drift, token-level distribution changes, and downstream metric delta (e.g., intent-accuracy for NLU customers).
Migration assistant UI: list affected customers, show compatibility score, suggested mitigation (pin, shim, multi-model fallback), estimated cost delta, and an automated notice action.

Orchestration: tie migration actions to release windows; allow scheduling of decommission phases (announce, nudge, lock, retire) with configurable dwell times and auto-fallback to alternate model variants.
Signals/telemetry: integrate with Console traces and Optimize gradients so alerts trigger when compatibility drops during rollouts.

communication_plan: Phase 1 (Internal beta): Invite solutions engineering and 10 pilot customers; collect feedback for 30 days.
Phase 2 (Public beta): Enable assistant for all Dedicated accounts and opt-in Hosted accounts with prominent console banner.
Phase 3 (GA): Automated scheduled decomm actions available and default 90-day notice window for non-enterprise customers.
Customer notices will follow a 4-message cadence: initial notice, migration suggestions with one-click pin, nudge + recommended deadline, final lock and deprecation confirmation.
migration_guides: Compatibility shim patterns (prompt adapters & response normalization): https://drive.redwood.ai/shims/prompt-adapters.pdf
customer_notice_samples: Initial notice (30d): We're retiring model variant 'rw-beta-2023-14' on 2025-04-15. The Console migration assistant shows low-risk replacements and a one-click pin option. See migration guide: <link>
Nudge (14d): We detected that your project uses the retiring variant. We recommend pinning to 'rw-stable-2.1' or running the compatibility assistant to confirm behavior. Pin now from Console.
Final (3d): Your project will be migrated to the replacement model on 2025-04-15 unless you pin a different variant. Contact support for exceptions.
tradeoffs_and_open_questions: How conservative should the compatibility score thresholds be for auto-scheduling rollouts? (initial proposal: >80 = safe, 60-80 = canary, <60 = manual review)
Privacy: can we reuse customer prompts for scoring or must we rely on synthetic/eval prompts? Need legal + security guidance.
Operational cost: running validator at scale (per-customer re-eval) may increase infra spend; consider sampling and incremental checks.
risks: False negatives: compatibility validator misses a regression and customers experience behavioral drift post-decommission.
Customer confusion: poorly timed notices could disrupt high-SLA customers; need clear SLA and manual-exempt flow.
Cost/latency: creating on-demand validation for thousands of customers could materially increase compute costs.
mitigations: Start with opt-in beta for Dedicated customers and high-touch accounts before enabling automated scheduling.
Require legal + security signoff for any plan that processes customer prompt data; fallback to synthetic evals when prohibited.
Expose cost estimates in assistant UI and cap auto-validation runs per customer by default.
metrics_and_success_criteria: Adoption: percent of targeted customers that interact with the assistant during beta (>40% target).
Regression rate: number of post-decommission incidents attributable to model drift (target <1 per quarter during pilot).
Time-to-migrate: median days between initial notice and either pin or scheduled rollout (target <21 days).
Cost: increase in compute spend for validation pipeline <10% relative to baseline during beta.
implementation_notes: Use existing re-eval infra from Optimize to compute embedding & response diffs; add a lightweight scoring layer tuned for false-positive reduction.
Compatibility validator should store anonymized evidence bundles (hashed input, candidate outputs, score) to make audits reproducible.
Console UI must allow customer success to flag 'do not auto-migrate' accounts and provide manual override logs.
